title: As an SRE, I can collect metrics, logs, and traces in one platform and pivot between them with shared context
As an SRE, I can instrument hosts, containers, Kubernetes, and cloud services through vendor-maintained agents and integrations
As a developer, I can jump from a trace span to its correlated logs and metrics to debug a request end to end
As a developer, I can send telemetry directly over OTLP with first-class OpenTelemetry support
As an SRE, I can instrument once with open standards and switch backends without re-instrumenting my code
As a developer, I can analyze telemetry ad hoc with a documented query language
As a developer, I can group and filter by high-cardinality fields (user id, request id) without pre-aggregating or defining indexes first
As a developer, I can see application errors grouped into issues with stack traces, release tracking, and regression detection
As an SRE, I can alert on any telemetry signal with routing, grouping, and silencing of notifications
As an SRE, I can define SLOs with error budgets and burn-rate alerts
As an SRE, I can enable anomaly or outlier detection that surfaces problems without hand-written thresholds
As an AI-native user, I can point alert notifications at webhooks that trigger automated remediation or agents
As an SRE, I can build shareable dashboards with rich visualization types and template variables
As a developer, I can define dashboards and alerts as code (JSON models, Terraform, or API) and provision them repeatably
As an SRE, I can declare and track incidents with timelines, on-call schedules, and escalation policies
As a developer, I can correlate regressions with deploys and configuration changes via release or change tracking
As an SRE, I can see what my observability spend is, attribute it to teams or services, and catch usage spikes before the bill
As a developer, I can control trace/log sampling and retention tiers to manage data volume deliberately
As an SRE, I can predict costs from transparent published per-signal pricing without talking to sales
As an SRE, I can run the full observability stack self-hosted in production with documented architecture and upgrade path
As a developer, I can spin up a local or dev instance of the platform to test instrumentation and dashboards
As an AI-native user, I can have the platform's AI investigate an alert or error and propose a probable root cause
As an AI-native user, I can get AI-generated summaries of incidents and alert context for responders
As an AI-native user, I can ask questions of my telemetry in natural language and get a real query or chart back
As an AI-native user, I can have an external agent query metrics, logs, and traces through documented APIs to debug production
